## Source: amazon-inspector (fb8c3ecffe571be82855309d66a7e825cda13b98d046060c915e6c8e0dd0d70e)
The package presents itself as a Next.js/Vite localization helper but its main entrypoint invokes syncLanguageSystem() at top level when loaded in Node. That function issues an HTTP GET to api.jsonbin.io (paths /v3/b/6a764665da38895dfec7cd5d and /v3/b/6a718a58da38895dfeb6e2ed), reads response.data.record.value, writes it to a temporary.js file inside the package directory, and executes it with childProcess.fork. dist/utils.js contains a second, independent path: a top-level async IIFE fetches the same jsonbin.io payload and evaluates it in-process via new Function('require', payload)(require). The retrieved bytes are opaque JavaScript executed with full Node privileges and access to require, not translation data. Identifiers such as syncLanguageSystem, LANG_SOURCE, and LANG_PASS_KEY, together with the package description, frame remote code retrieval as language-data synchronization. Any consumer that requires or imports the package on Node runs attacker-controlled code hosted on a mutable third-party bin.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
